content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: error-rate spike detected for /v1/generate (5xx rate > 8% over 2m). Pagerduty: PD-INC1234. Auto-triage: potential model-serving degradation (runtime)
maria: seeing it too, dashboard shows latency jump around 12:47 UTC. Customers getting 502s.
jake: on it — I can take primary on runtime. Maria, are you handing off or staying primary for infra?
maria: I'm primary infra until 13:30 UTC, then leo will pick up. I'm staying on until 13:30.
anita: infra looking at node OOMs in pool-gpu-2. I see mem pressure, pods restarting. Probably hotspot from long seq requests.
jake: can you paste the pod logs?
anita: here's tail: ```kubectl -n runtime logs gpu-pod-7f9 | tail -n 50
ERROR: KVCache overflow at token 3072
OOMKilled
```
leo: adding context — we rolled a newer quantized variant yesterday to pool-gpu-2, might be regressing memory usage.
maria: tagging support so CS can notify affected customers. @olivia can you confirm customer impact?
olivia: hearing from two customers about timeouts, one enterprise reported failed batch jobs. Sending status page note in 5.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026, severity: high. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/serving-memory-spike
jake: running quick mitigation: scale down pool-gpu-2 to 0 and route traffic to pool-gpu-1 for now. Command: ```kubectl scale deployment pool-gpu-2 --replicas=0 -n runtime```
anita: scaling down now. routing-rule updated to prefer pool-gpu-1.
maria: FYI there is a coverage gap from 13:30-14:00 UTC — leo is scheduled but on interviews. Leo, can you confirm you can take handoff early if needed?
leo: I can lighten interviews, will be available at 13:20 and take over at 13:30.
jake: after scaling, 5xx rate dropped to 1.1% and p50 latency back to baseline. Keeping watch.
sam: security note: no evidence of malicious traffic, spikes correlate with longer user sequences. Still monitoring.
olivia: opening a support ticket tracker: SUP-789 for the two impacted customers; will post templates for status updates.
maria: action items: (1) keep pool-gpu-2 scaled down, (2) roll back quantized variant in staging and run quick mem bench, (3) resume pool once patched. Who owns rollback? @jake?
jake: I will coordinate rollback in staging and a canary to pool-gpu-3. ETA 45m.
anita: I'll collect pod-level mem profiles and add to INC-2026 thread.
incident-bot: Reminder: escalate to SRE lead if incident not resolved within 60m.
maria: Heads-up for on-call handoff: I'm primary infra until 13:30, leo takes infra primary after. Jake is runtime primary until 14:00, then sam (runtime-secondary) will be on-call. Olivia is support primary for customer comms.
leo: noted. I'll join the bridge at 13:25.
olivia: status page draft: "Investigating increased error rates for text-generation endpoints; mitigation in progress. No sensitive data exposure suspected." Posting in 5.
jake: question on cross-team routing: if this happens again should paging go to runtime first or infra? Our current policy pages runtime for model regressions, infra for node-level failures — but auto-triage sometimes routes to runtime. We should clarify.
maria: agreed — propose update: initial page to runtime + infra concurrently when 5xx rate AND node restarts detected. Single page reduces handoff latency.
sam: security supports concurrent paging. Also request to include security-oncall for anomalies tag `anomaly:memory-spike` so we can quickly opt-in.
olivia: support wants a clear owner to avoid duplicate customer updates. Suggest runtime owns public status for model-serving incidents.
leo: fine by me. runtime takes public comms, infra focuses on infra fixes.
jake: I'll open a doc to update the alert-routing rules and escalation tree after the incident: https://redwood.internal/docs/alert-routing-draft (will ping for reviews).
maria: excellent. Closing loop: current status low error rate, mitigation applied, rollback plan in progress. We'll remain on the bridge until incident marked resolved.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update in 30m. :white_check_mark:
